column1: # Applicability matrix: which techniques are demanded per target class, and which
# instruments can satisfy each. `n_a` rows are never demanded and never counted as
# MISSED -- this is what stops the ledger asking for halmos on Anchor.
# A technique with applicability=applies and NO available instrument still applies.
# That is deliberate: the absence of an instrument is a gap worth a recorded reason,
# not a reason to silently drop the row. Decline it; do not hide it.

column5: rationale
Solidity sources are available for every EVM program in scope.
Mature Solidity detector suites exist and are installed.
Three independent property fuzzers target Solidity; any one satisfies the technique.
ItyFuzz is the only coverage-guided EVM fuzzer we hold; pinned Linux container only.
Halmos runs directly on Foundry tests; Mythril does symbolic bytecode analysis.
Foundry is the native EVM test runner.
Sibling/twin contracts and upgrade pairs are the common EVM shape.
Deployed bytecode yields ABI, payability, and value-opcode enumeration.
Public RPC exposes storage, code, and forkable real state.
Value flows and attacker cycle costs must be modeled explicitly.
Solidity projects vendor libraries whose provenance is in scope.
Rust/Anchor sources are available for programs in scope.
Radar is Anchor-aware; Semgrep takes custom Rust rules; clippy is a weak third.
Trident is the Anchor property fuzzer; a Mollusk arbitrary-session runner is the fallback.
cargo-fuzz/libfuzzer-sys is the Rust coverage-guided path.
No Solana/SBF symbolic executor exists in our runtime. The technique still applies; the gap is declined with a reason, never silently dropped. EVM solvers are not substitutes.
Mollusk executes the exact ELF against local accounts.
Program twins, forged-ID twins, and version diffs are the common Anchor shape.
The SBF ELF is the shipped artifact; source alone does not settle enumeration.
Live program accounts, upgrade authority, and config are readable over RPC.
Rent, fees, and CPI composition change what an exit is worth.
Crate provenance and unsafe surface are in scope.
Go sources are available for modules in scope.
Go has mature static analysers; filter generated protobuf before quoting counts.
Go native fuzzing covers property campaigns.
Go native fuzzing is coverage-guided by construction.
No Go symbolic executor is held. Applies; must be declined with a reason.
Go test is the native runner.
Fork/version divergence is the common Cosmos shape.
Go modules ship as source in scope; no separate compiled artifact is adjudicated.
Chain state and module params are readable over RPC.
Gas, fees, and inter-module composition govern impact.
Module provenance and pinned toolchain are in scope.
Always applicable where source exists.
Semgrep is language-agnostic enough to always apply.
Without a declared property surface this cannot be demanded generically.
Requires a harnessable entry point that a generic target may not have.
No general-purpose solver path for arbitrary targets.
Any reproduction attempt counts.
Version and sibling comparison always applies.
No compiled artifact is assumed.
The live instance is usually reachable.
Impact model is target-specific and cannot be demanded generically.
Dependency provenance always applies.
